reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes sinless righteousness, which Ecclesiastes denies of all but Christ, from the imputed righteousness by which scripture still calls other men just.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible sets Ecclesiastes' denial that any just man exists against the roster of named figures — Noah, Lot, Joseph, Simeon, John the Baptist, Joseph of Arimathea, Cornelius — the Bible itself calls just.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Has there ever been a just person?"

sides.snippet: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time.
sides.verseText: This is the history of the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.

sides.snippet: there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn't sin.
sides.verseText: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn't sin.
